text:
maria_cs: Quick heads-up — prepping a renewal QBR for Cartella. onboarding slipped 3 weeks, they’re still on a dev key and we saw a big token spike last Friday. need a short runbook: forecast, quick mitigations, and a token econ slide. cc @dylan_finops @alex_se

dylan_finops: got it. can someone drop the last 30d burn + a 30/60/90 forecast? i’ll sketch conservative vs aggressive comms and a credits recommendation.

noah_data: pulling numbers now. quick summary: 30d tokens = 1,240,500; avg tokens/req = 210; peak day = 420k tokens (embed batch job). preliminary 30/60/90 baseline forecast: 1.5M / 1.9M / 2.3M. burst scenario (no throttles): 3.8M in 30d.

jenna_csm: onboarding status: SSO still pending, using dev key, scheduled integration finish Apr 5. renewal window = 45 days. they asked for monthly spend predictability.

alex_se: immediate mitigations i recommend: 1) enforce dev-key read-only & rotate to prod key on go-live 2) set quota at 70% of current committed for alerts 3) enable prefix caching for embed IDs 4) reduce embedding batch size to avoid big single-job spikes. small change to client config: 
```json
{"embeddings_batch_size": 16, "cache_ttl": 3600}
```

maria_cs: can we get a one-slide token econ calc? dylan, add commit/retainer options. we want to present 2 options: (A) credits safety-net + 10% buffer (B) monthly commit + lower unit price + auto-burst holdback.

dylan_finops: drafting slide. rough calc: baseline 1.5M tokens * $0.0005 per 1k = $750/month baseline. aggressive buffer -> ~3.8M => ~$1,900. propose safety-net of $2k prepaid credits for month 1 and a monthly retainer option of $1,200 with overage at lower tier. i’ll formalize numbers.

noah_data: uploaded spreadsheet excerpt to drive (link) — includes daily burn series and top endpoints by token. top offender = /embed/bulk with average 40k tokens/job.

jenna_csm: client is sensitive to surprise charges. suggest we offer a staged rollout: keep strict quotas until SSO + prod key confirmed, then relax. i’ll own comms.

budgetbot: Alert created: cartella-credits-threshold @ 70% (subscriber: customer-success).

alex_se: also recommend we ship a small eval: a short-lived rate-limit rule for the dev key: max 10 reqs/min and per-day token cap 250k until go-live. ops can push via config: 
```bash
redwoodctl set-policy --key cartella-dev --rate 10/m --daily-tokens 250000
```

maria_cs: timeline for deliverables: noah — final forecast CSV by EOD; dylan — slide + two pricing options by EOD; alex — PR for config rule + rollback plan by EOD; jenna — client note draft by EOD. we’ll sync 9am tomorrow for final QBR agenda.

dylan_finops: noted. will include a short slide showing cost sensitivity to embed batch size and suggested guardrail language for renewal.

jenna_csm: i’ll include customer feedback bullets: fragility of dev key, confusion about embed batching, ask for quota transparency dashboard.

maria_cs: perfect. low-friction ask: add a one-click “temporary credits top-up” option in the billing page for CS to propose in call. tagging product later. :thumbsup:

budgetbot: Reminder scheduled: QBR-draft-review at 2024-04-02T16:00:00Z (created by maria_cs).

alex_se: PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/policies/1234 (drafted rules + unit tests). please review.

noah_data: uploaded final forecast CSV. figures match earlier: conservative baseline 1.5M, planned buffer 2.1M, burst 3.8M.

maria_cs: thanks team. will compile and share with customer 24h before meeting. short notes for the call: show baseline, show mitigations (dev-key quotas + cache + batch tuning), present 2 cost options, offer temporary credits top-up.

jenna_csm: copying final action items into the customer-facing note now.

maria_cs: closing thread — we’ll pick up tomorrow in sync. :wave:
